Scope the target.\n- Identify method boundaries, collaborator behavior, side effects, and invariants.\n- Identify which tests cover the method today.\n\n2. Run baseline coverage.\n- For core targets, prefer `scripts/method_coverage_report.py` when available.\n- For add-on targets, prefer `scripts/addon_method_coverage_report.py` when available.\n- If coverage scripts are unavailable, use PHPUnit coverage output and compute method-level gaps manually.\n\n3. Close coverage gaps (tests only).\n- Add focused tests until `target_method` reaches 100% line and 100% branch coverage.\n- Cover happy path, branch alternatives, boundaries, failures, and side effects.\n- Keep test names behavior-focused and deterministic.\n\n4. Freeze and commit tests.\n- Run the target test command and ensure it passes.\n- Record the exact command(s) used to verify the method.\n- Stage only test/support changes and create a dedicated test commit.\n- Suggested commit message: `tests(refactor-lock): cover <Class>::<method> to 100%`\n\n5. Apply comment style rules.\n- Add comments only where intent is non-obvious.\n- Use concise, implementation-relevant comments.\n- For multi-line comments, use a tapered style where each next line is 3 characters shorter than the previous line.\n- Use `...` when needed to satisfy the 3-character taper rule.\n\nExample tapered comment:\n```php\n// Validate account state before mutation...\n// Validate account state before mut...\n// Validate account state before...\n```\n\n7. Verify without touching tests.\n- Run the same frozen test command(s) from phase 4.\n- If any frozen test fails, continue refactoring production code only until they pass.\n- If passing requires changing tests, stop and report a blocker instead of editing tests.\n\n8.
